summary: An agent asks the user for a secret through the Switchboard MCP tool request_secret. The chat shows a card with a masked input; Switchboard writes the value to a private 0600 file for that chat only and tells the agent the file path and the env var SWITCHBOARD_SECRETS_DIR, never the value. Step 1: the file store (main/secrets/secret-store.ts) and the agent_secret_dirs and agent_secrets tables. Step 2: the request_secret tool on the MCP server while the flag is on (refused in plan mode, from an open child chat, past 3 open cards or 5 requests in 10 minutes, and for any unknown or out-of-range field), sbsec_ cards in the approval card broker (request.opened.secretRequest, a plain detail with no title for older clients and push), saves only through ProviderRegistry.answerAgentSecret (a failed save keeps the card open; an approval on the generic respond channel is refused), result turns with the path and env var, SWITCHBOARD_SECRETS_DIR in every agent kind's env at session start, a Stop that keeps the card and the files, an archive that closes the card and deletes the files, and extend and delete now. Step 3 (this change): the desktop card (renderer SecretRequestCard: header, title, plain-text instructions with the URL host in bold and an open confirm, an uncontrolled password input with a 10-second show button, Save securely and Decline, the footer with the ttl and the SSH machine, the provider-key note), its answer channel agent-secret:answer, extend, delete and list (admin scope, strict argument shapes, flag-gated, Extend and Delete now only on the asking chat's own secrets, list without values), the channels kept out of perf spans and the reconnect queue, and the one-line Saved, Declined and expired states with Extend and Delete now.

desktop.followUpRelease: The release that turns agent_secret_request on (design section 12, step 6). Redaction of a printed value (step 4) comes before that.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: Design section 12, step 5: a read-only card with Decline and Answer this on your computer. No phone enters a secret in v1.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: Design section 12, step 5: the same read-only card as the Expo app.

sharedBackendApi.followUpRelease: Design section 12, step 6 turns the flag on. Step 3 (this change) adds the agent-secret:answer, extend, delete and list channels (admin scope on every host), capability agent_secret_request_v1, and their exclusion from perf spans and the WsTransport reconnect queue.

automated: tests/unit/secret-store.test.ts: folder modes (root 0700, chat folder 0300 and not listable, file 0600), Spotlight marker and backup exclusion, exact bytes with no .partial left, name and size rules, a symlink at the .partial path is refused and its target untouched, a second save replaces the file and retires the old row, a failed record deletes the file, extend, delete now, expiry by timer, archive removes files, folder and dir row, the sweep removes expired files, orphan folders, .partial and unknown files and keeps live ones, and the folder and rows follow a session id rotation to the root conversation.

tests/unit/secret-request-tool.test.ts: argument rules (unknown field, name, title, instructions, ttl), the saved text names the path and the env var, plan mode, open child and bad arguments open no card, 3 open cards and 5 requests per 10 minutes, the broker saves only through saveSecret and keeps the card open when the save throws, a Stop skips secret cards, and the push text holds no title or instructions.

tests/unit/secret-request-registry.test.ts: with the flag off no tool and no env var; with it on the tool is listed and the session env has SWITCHBOARD_SECRETS_DIR; a save tells the agent the path and the env var and the value is in no event, row or turn; a failed save keeps the card open; decline; an approval on RESPOND_TO_REQUEST is refused and a deny closes it; a Stop keeps the card, an archive closes it and removes the chat's files.

tests/unit/secret-request-registry.test.ts (answer channel): save and decline through agent-secret:answer, every malformed answer shape refused with the card kept open, every channel refused with the flag off, list returns metadata and a status and never the value, extend and delete refused for another chat's secret and for a missing id.

tests/unit/agent-secret-channels-private.test.ts: every agent-secret channel is marked as carrying a secret, is never wrapped in a perf span, is refused (not queued) by a disconnected WsTransport, needs the admin scope (phone, pr-write and terminal credentials refused), and the capability is advertised.

tests/unit/secret-request-card.test.ts (jsdom): header without the product name, host in bold, password input with new-password, spellcheck and autocorrect off and no value attribute, Save off until a value fits, trim note, keys stop at the card, 10-second show, Save clears the field and sends the trimmed value once, a refused answer keeps the card with its message, Decline sends no value, the provider-key note, and the saved line's time left, Extend in place and Delete now.

tests/unit/secret-request-card-model.test.ts: footer and countdown texts, trim, UTF-8 byte count, the 16 KiB limit, URL splitting (user part not shown as the host), provider-key match, collapsed state mapping, and the answer shape check.
hardware: The migration ran against a copy of a real 1.1 GB profile database (1,450 conversations): both tables were created and PRAGMA integrity_check answered ok.
notExercised: tmutil addexclusion was not checked against a real Time Machine setup; tests inject the exclusion step.

Codex sandbox modes (read-only, workspace-write) read any file by default and Claude's sandbox mode prompts per tool with no OS sandbox, so no read allow list was added; this was read from the adapters, not run.

No packaged build has run the card yet (high-risk rule): the save, extend and delete paths were checked by unit and jsdom tests only, not on a packaged app with existing user data or through a real SSH tunnel.
The card's look in the dark, light and translucent themes was not compared against the mock in a screenshot test.
